blocks.text: Group 2 metals react with dilute acids to give a salt and hydrogen gas, and reactivity increases down the group. Beryllium reacts with dilute acids to form BeCl2 and hydrogen, though its oxide layer can slow the reaction. Magnesium reacts readily with dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid, and calcium reacts vigorously: Ca(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> CaCl2(aq) + H2(g).

blocks.title: Calcium and sulphuric acid
blocks.text: With sulphuric acid the reaction of calcium can stop early, because the calcium sulphate formed is sparingly soluble and coats the metal with a protective layer.

blocks.prompt: Write equations for (i) calcium with oxygen and (ii) barium with water.
Predict how the density and melting point of radium might compare with barium.
blocks.explanation: Following the trend, radium should be denser than barium (above 3.51 g/cm3); the melting points fall irregularly from Ca to Ba, so radium's melting point would be expected to be similar to or a little below barium's.
